title: How a polymer filling enhances the rate and selectivity of colloid permeation across mesopores
authors: Mikhail Y. Laktionov, Frans A. M. Leermakers, Ralf P. Richter, Leonid I. Klushin, Oleg V. Borisov
abstract: Polymer-functionalised mesopores are an emerging technology for colloid separation, sensing and delivery. Their potential is strikingly illustrated in living cells, where nuclear pore complexes (NPCs) control biocolloid transport between the nucleus and the cytosol. Even colloids much smaller than the biopolymer-filled NPC channel are effectively blocked, but some larger colloids with distinct surface features rapidly permeate. Simplistically, one may expect any polymer filling to obstruct and slow down colloid transport. We demonstrate how a polymer filling that attracts colloids and extends beyond the mesopore, thus maximizing colloid capture, can instead increase permeation compared to a bare pore. We also define how polymer-filled mesopores can effectively gate colloids according to their size and surface features. Our findings provide a basic physical explanation for the exquisite permselectivity of NPCs, and a rational design strategy for novel mesopore-based separation, sensing, catalysis and drug delivery devices with enhanced performance features.
summary: This work develops a theoretical framework to model how polymer coatings inside mesopores control the passage of colloids. By treating the process as an electrical resistance problem, the authors show that polymer attraction can enhance, rather than just impede, transport. This provides a physical basis for understanding highly selective biological barriers like the Nuclear Pore Complex.
main_problem: The study investigates how polymer filling within mesopores affects the rate and selectivity of colloid permeation, aiming to explain the exquisite permselectivity observed in Nuclear Pore Complexes (NPCs).
main_result: The theoretical framework demonstrates that polymer filling can enhance transport beyond bare pores by maximizing colloid capture, providing a rational design strategy for separation devices.
method: The authors employ theoretical methods, reformulating the diffusion problem into calculating the total electrical resistance of a medium with position-dependent resistivity.
model_or_system: The model uses a cylinder-shaped mesopore filled with a polymer brush, drawing inspiration from the biophysical system of the NPC. Transport is governed by the Smoluchowski equation, treated via electrical analogy.
key_observables: Stationary diffusive flux (j), total pore resistance (R), and the partition coefficient (P) for colloids.
important_parameters: Polymer grafting density ($\sigma$), degree of polymerization ($N$), Flory-Huggins parameter ($\chi$), and colloid diameter ($d$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes unidirectional transport driven by concentration differences and uses simplified models for the pore geometry and colloid shape.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of colloid transport through a polymer brush-filled pore and show theoretical predictions mapped against experimental data for NPC translocation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical system (polymer-filled mesopores/NPCs) to establishing the governing mathematical framework (electrical analogy for diffusion) and finally applying this theory to derive quantitative relationships for transport rates and selectivity.
why_interesting: While focused on soft matter transport, the use of resistance/conductivity analogies to model diffusion in complex, confined media touches upon non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and transport phenomena relevant to open quantum systems.
